nodes.title: Note: Usage
widgets_values:
## No-reference scoring (no clean reference needed)

Both `LoadImage` nodes feed `BatchImagesNode`, so the SAME batch runs through
three no-reference metrics - the quickest way to compare models on identical
input:

- **pyiqa NR Score** with A-FINE (NR head): **lower is better**, range ~-2 to 2.
- **FGResQ NR Score** with the FGResQ NR variant: **higher is better**, 0-1.
- **QReAlign NR Score** with Q-ReAlign Mini 0.8B (int8_convrot), task
  `aesthetic IAA`: **higher is better**, 0-1. This one judges aesthetics, not
  technical fidelity.

Each score node is per image (`OUTPUT_IS_LIST`), so two images in produce two
values - the Preview widgets show a list.

## How to run

1. Point the two `LoadImage` nodes at your own images (any size; the pack handles
   each architecture's constraints, e.g. A-FINE needs sides divisible by 32).
2. Queue the prompt - no reference image is involved.
3. Read the three Preview widgets.

The first run downloads weights into `ComfyUI/models/pyiqa/` (or a pyiqa folder
from `extra_model_paths.yaml`): A-FINE ~580 MB, FGResQ ~1.2 GB (two files),
Q-ReAlign Mini int8 ~1.6 GB. Q-ReAlign also needs `transformers>=5`; if yours is
older the loader stops and prints the exact `pip install` command.

## Why three metrics fit in VRAM at once

All three score nodes are set to `memory_management = unload model (VRAM + RAM)`,
so each metric releases its weights the moment it has scored - they never occupy
VRAM together. `Unload Pyiqa Models` at the end empties whatever is left; it is a
passthrough, so it can sit on any wire (here it carries the Q-ReAlign score to its
Preview). Switch a score node to `keep loaded` when scoring many images in a row:
reloading for every image is what makes it slow.
